story.what_it_does: IEX runs an online marketplace where electricity, green certificates (RECs) and, through its IGX unit, gas are bought and sold. It earns money from fees on the volumes traded. It also has early plans for coal and carbon trading.
story.plans: Management aims for about 15% electricity volume growth in FY27 and expects the real-time market to grow 25-30% a year, though that is a gut feeling. It also targets 40-50% volume growth at IGX this year, plans to start carbon trading by 1 October 2026, and is looking at a coal exchange and battery storage.
story.moat: IEX is the dominant exchange, with a stated 99.2% share of the day-ahead and real-time markets in Q2 FY27. The notes do not describe any other moat in detail. Market coupling, which would make Grid India the sole coupling operator, is a regulatory threat to this position.

scenarios.story: Volumes keep growing at 15% or more, with real-time market growth of 25-30%, while IGX, carbon and coal trading add new income. Market coupling is stopped or goes ahead without hurting IEX's share.
signals_to_watch: Real-time market share of electricity volumes (41% in H1 FY27) keeps rising
Carbon trading starts by 1 October 2026 and IGX volume growth reaches 40-50%

scenarios.story: Electricity volumes grow in the mid-teens, as in Q2 FY27 (12.7%) and H1 FY27 (14.2%), and profit grows roughly with revenue (Q2 profit up 12.9%). The REC business stays small and market coupling remains unresolved.
signals_to_watch: Quarterly electricity volume growth versus the 15% FY27 expectation
Revenue and profit growth in coming quarters (Q2 FY27 revenue up 10.7%, PAT up 12.9%)

scenarios.story: Market coupling goes ahead with Grid India as sole operator, and IEX loses market share, which management would not quantify. REC volumes stay weak and higher prices could dampen demand.
signals_to_watch: Court outcome on IEX's challenge to the CERC market coupling order in APTEL and the Supreme Court
